hero.subtitle: A collision on Peck Road or the I-10 can upend an ordinary week in El Monte. We connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency.

about.title: El Monte Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Peck Road, Valley Boulevard, Lower Azusa Road and the I-10 through El Monte carry a lot of daily traffic, and the public record reflects it: in 2025 the city logged 539 injury collisions, with 753 people hurt and 5 lives lost. Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. tend to be when reports cluster, often as commuters head home. If one of those crashes was yours, you may be dealing with pain, a totaled car and an adjuster who keeps calling. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects El Monte residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most drivers two years to file, but claims involving a public agency can require action in as little as six months. The sooner evidence like dashcam footage, witness contacts and repair estimates is gathered, the stronger your position tends to be.

whyChoose.title: What an Independent Attorney Brings to Your El Monte Claim

items.title: Your Filing Window Is Real
items.desc: California allows two years for most car accident lawsuits, yet a claim against a city, county or state agency can carry a six-month deadline. An attorney sorts out which clock applies to your crash and calendars it early.

items.title: Shared Blame Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible; your compensation is simply reduced by your share. An attorney pushes back when an insurer tries to inflate that percentage.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Fee
items.desc: California places no statutory cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in ordinary car accident cases. Network attorneys work on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not obligated to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurance company. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to minimize your claim. Most attorneys prefer you speak with them first, and many will handle that communication for you.

items.question: I was hit on the I-10 near the Peck Road exit. Does the location change anything?
items.answer: It can. Freeway crashes are usually documented by the California Highway Patrol rather than El Monte police, so the report is requested differently. If road design, signage or a government vehicle played any role, a shorter six-month claim deadline may apply, which is one more reason to get an attorney reviewing the facts promptly.

items.question: What should I be saving right now?
items.answer: Hold onto photos of the vehicles and scene, the exchange-of-information sheet, medical discharge papers, receipts and any texts or emails with insurers. Keep your damaged car unrepaired until it has been photographed, and jot down the names of anyone who saw the crash. Evidence like nearby business camera footage can be overwritten within days, so acting quickly matters.
